title: A red end run is bisected over the sprint's landings by backlog.py bisect, and kb-sprint says what to do with the culprit
goal: a new backlog.py subcommand finds the landed commit after which the failing test ids first fail, as a git bisect run script that exits 0, 1 or 125 and counts a step bad only when the failure repeats on a re-run at that commit, holding the host lock; kb-sprint says to file a bug naming that commit's item and dispatch a kb-worker for it at once, or, when the commit's KB-Work trailer names an item outside the sprint, to file it against that item's sprint and tell its owner; planted tests: a red end run finds the culprit landing, a failure that does not repeat on a re-run is not counted bad, and a culprit whose item lies outside the sprint is routed to its owner; the new module follows the new-module rule
